It was never hard to predict that most Venezuelans would oppose this deal. Most Americans should too. Putting Chevron in control of a substantial portion of the development, production and commercialization of Venezuela's oil reserves may be great for Chevron's shareholders, but it does nothing for American workers or the middle class. As it is, most Venezuelan oil is already processed in the US.

The point is that the only sustainable way to make Americans collectively richer is to increase the productivity of American workers, and unless Chevron sells all this oil to Americans at well below world prices (which I doubt either Caracas or Chevron's shareholders will allow), its control over Venezuelan reserves will not increase the value of goods and services produced in the US. In fact to the extent that the resulting net inflows strengthen the dollar, it might actually further undermine manufacturing in the US.

The administration should be focused  on building industry at home, and not on boosting the foreign profits of American companies.
